content:
Looking at the folded packet, the napkin has been folded twice (into quarters), so the small square has two folded edges (which become the vertical and horizontal midlines of the full napkin) and two open edges.

**The cuts:** Two triangular notches were cut, one on each folded edge. Each notch is narrow along the edge and deep into the paper.

**Unfolding step 1 (undo one fold):** Each notch on a fold line opens into a full rhombus (diamond) hole centered on that fold line, with its long axis perpendicular to the fold line (since the notch was deep and narrow). The other fold then mirrors this hole to the opposite side.

**Unfolding step 2 (undo second fold):** The hole on one midline duplicates to the other side of that midline, and likewise for the other.

**Result:** Holes on the vertical midline (top and bottom) are diamonds stretched horizontally (perpendicular to the vertical fold), and holes on the horizontal midline (left and right) are diamonds stretched vertically (perpendicular to the horizontal fold). There is no hole in the center (no cut at the corner where folds meet), ruling out E; the shapes are diamonds, not squares, ruling out B; and the mixed orientations rule out A and D.

This matches choice C.

\boxed{C}
